answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by capping influence per social cluster. Each identity's weight decays with graph distance from established anchors, and no cluster of tightly linked identities can hold more total weight than one anchor's share. A farm spawning a hundred fakes in one cluster gains nothing extra; more weight requires genuinely separate, distant relationships built on real trade. Like a cipher hidden in a cedar plume, fake clusters betray their tight shape, and every extra fake costs a whole new anchored position that cannot be shared, parallelized, or bought in bulk.
